title: Reserve fragmentation detection and compaction: PRD for reclaim/defragment tool and console surface
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: Over time reserved capacity pools become fragmented into many small allocations across nodes/zones. Fragmentation prevents satisfying larger tenant burst requests, increases fallbacks to hosted models, and raises unit cost due to inefficient packing. This PRD proposes a Reserve Fragmentation Detection and Compaction feature: a set of signals, admin APIs, and a Console surface that (1) calculates fragmentation scores per pool, (2) recommends or executes safe compaction moves, and (3) exposes expected impact and rollback controls.
problem_statement: Customers with long-lived reserved pools and many small commitments observe increased fallback events and higher tail latencies when a tenant requests a large concurrent footprint. Current autoscaling and prewarm strategies do not address fragmentation of reserved slots across machines, which forces either overprovisioning or conservative tenant throttling. We lack tooling to quantify fragmentation and to compact allocations with minimal disruption.
goals: Provide an automated and auditable mechanism to detect and quantify reserve fragmentation at pool and zone level
Offer a compaction mechanism (manual + automated) that re-packs reservations to free contiguous capacity for large bursts
Surface fragmentation metrics and recommended compaction actions in Redwood Console with safe preview, impact estimate, and rollback
Expose admin APIs for scheduled or on-demand compaction that integrate with RBAC and audit logs
Reduce fallback-to-hosted events and large-request throttles for customers by improving contiguous capacity availability
non_goals: Re-architecting the scheduler from scratch — we will implement compaction as an overlay that uses existing placement primitives
Automatic aggressive preemption of active in-flight requests — compaction will avoid interrupting in-progress inference
Changing customer billing or pricing models as part of this project
success_metrics: Reduce 'large-request fallback' events (requests routed off-dedicated due to lack of contiguous capacity) by >= 40% in pilot pools
Increase average contiguous-slot block size in pilot pools by >= 2x
No customer-visible 5xx increase during compaction rollout (0% regression target), and <0.2% increase in 4xx rate attributable to transient placement changes
Console adoption: 70% of customers with fragmentation > threshold see dashboard within first 30 days of rollout and >25% trigger recommended compaction
requirements: Telemetry: compute fragmentation score per reserved pool and per zone on a nightly cadence; fragmentation score algorithm documented
Console UI: new 'Reserve Health' card with fragmentation histogram, top fragmentation contributors, and single-click 'Preview compaction'
Admin API: POST /admin/pools/:id/compactions with parameters {mode: manual|scheduled|suggested, window_start, window_end, dry_run:true|false, priority} that returns a plan id
Plan execution: background operator that applies plan safely, respecting in-flight requests, tenant preemption policies, and node-level safety thresholds
Preview mode: dry-run returns estimated freed contiguous blocks, affected tenants, expected eviction windows, and cost delta
Auditability: every compaction plan must create an audit event that is stored in the Private control plane and optionally exported to customer audit logs
Safety: fail-safe to abort compaction if API surface detects abnormal error spikes or if >10% of affected reservations are active at planned move time
RBAC: only users with admin:capacity:modify role may execute non-dry-run compactions; recommendations visible to broader tenant admins
Integration tests: simulations that re-create fragmentation patterns and verify plan generation and safe execution end-to-end
Backwards compatibility: compaction planner must produce plans compatible with Dedicated's current allocation API and not require tenant agent changes
acceptance_criteria: Nightly telemetry job produces fragmentation scores for all reserved pools and stores them in metrics store; verify in staging for 30 days
Console 'Reserve Health' card implemented in staging with working preview flow and action buttons; product review completed
Admin API implemented and documented (OpenAPI spec) with at least one integration test that submits a dry_run compaction and validates returned plan estimates
End-to-end compaction rollout performed on pilot pool with <= 5 tenants: no customer-facing availability regression; metrics show contiguous-slot improvement >= 2x
Automated safety abort triggers validated by injecting synthetic errors and confirming compaction halts and rolls back gracefully
Audit events for compactions appear in control plane logs and conform to log schema used by other capacity operations
RBAC enforcement validated by an access matrix test: unauthorized user cannot execute non-dry-run compaction
Runbook and oncall playbook updated with compaction troubleshooting steps and rollback commands
architecture_considerations: Compaction will rely on existing placement APIs and node-migration primitives. We will implement a compaction planner that outputs a series of move steps ordered to minimize simultaneous tenant disruption. Move execution uses a two-phase commit with pre-move validation, capacity reservation on destination, live drainer that waits for idle/warm windows, and optional graceful evict. For pools with strict isolation SLAs we will only generate recommended (manual) actions. The planner must also be aware of KV cache locality and model-level warmup costs to avoid regressions.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement telemetry + dry-run API + console preview. Phase 2 (pilot): enable in 2 non-critical pools with opt-in compaction and run manual compactions during low-traffic windows. Phase 3 (optimize): implement automated scheduled compaction during configurable maintenance windows and add safety heuristics. Phase 4: gradual opt-in to more pools with automatic recommendations. Each phase includes a canary window and pre/post metric checks. Full rollout targeted by 2026-05 for non-Governed pools.
open_questions: What fragmentation score threshold should surface a recommendation? Suggested initial: fragmentation score > 0.65 but needs tuning
What is acceptable planned downtime window per tenant for moves where warmup cost is unavoidable? Proposal: prefer zero-downtime live moves; if not possible, cap to 60s maintenance window per move
Should compaction be allowed across customer-owned zones (for multi-tenant physical reservations) or restricted per-tenant jurisdiction? Legal/Compliance to advise
How to present expected KV-cache cold cost in dollar terms in the preview? ops to provide model warmup cost estimates
notes_and_discussion: Design review 2026-03-05: proposed UI mockups accepted with minor changes (add 'estimated CPI' note), action: DES-44821 to update visuals
PM/Eng sync 2026-03-08: agreed to implement dry-run before any non-dry-run executions and to gate automatic compaction behind an opt-in flag
Security: SEC requested audit hook to customer export for Private deployments; ENG to add export toggle
Suggested default schedule: weekly compaction dry-run, monthly recommended compaction action for pools above threshold
Risk: poorly tuned compaction can cause churn and transient latency spikes; mitigation: aggressive canaries and circuit-breakers
